# parity-fuzz --mode cond baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode cond --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# Covers the `test` / `[` builtin: unary flags, the three-argument binary-
# operator form, `-a`/`-o` connectives, `!`, and parenthesised groups. Both
# spellings are generated — one builtin under two funcids (BIN_TEST=20 /
# BIN_BRACKET=21, c:Src/builtin.c:7231-7247). stderr is folded into stdout
# because the diagnostics are as much the contract as the status, and the
# status alone cannot tell 1 (false) from 2 (error).
#
# ONE known gap. Every signature below is the SAME shape: the literal string
# `-a` (or `-n`) used as an OPERAND next to a connective, where which token is
# the operator is genuinely ambiguous —
#
#     test -a -a -a  → zsh 0 (middle `-a` is the connective, outer two are
#                             non-empty strings), zshrs 1
#     test '' -a -a  → zsh 1,  zshrs error
#     test ! -a      → zsh 1,  zshrs error
#     test -a a      → zsh "too many arguments" rc=2, zshrs 0
#
# C resolves these for free because it never scans for a connective: bin_test
# does only the XSI argument-count fixups and then hands the list to the real
# grammar (c:7276-7280 `condlex = testlex; testlex(); parse_cond()`), which
# consumes tokens in order — so position, not spelling, decides what is an
# operator. par_cond_2 (c:Src/parse.c:2478-2515) supplies the POSIX rules by
# ARGUMENT COUNT: n_testargs == 1 makes `[ foo ]` into `[ -n foo ]`, and
# n_testargs > 2 treats the SECOND argument as binary only when it really is
# one (`=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`, `-<condnum>`), otherwise falling through.
#
# zshrs cannot reach any of that. bin_test is an ad-hoc argument-count parser;
# the real grammar is unreachable because `testlex` is DEAD CODE (nothing
# references it) and par_cond_2 hardcodes `let n_testargs: i32 = 0;`, disabling
# the POSIX-test rule set it ports. Same faithful-port-shadowed-by-a-
# reimplementation shape as (D)/substnamedir and typeset_single. The fix is to
# wire testlex + par_cond with a real n_testargs — NOT to add more
# argument-count branches or more connective-scanning to the ad-hoc parser,
# which is exactly what cannot express these.
#
# Scope, measured rather than assumed: every COMMON idiom passes —
# `[ -f x -a -d y ]`, `[ -n a -o -n b ]`, three-way chains, `-a`/`-o`
# precedence, `[ ! -f x -a -d y ]`, `[ 1 -eq 1 -a 2 -eq 2 ]`. What is left needs
# `-a`/`-n` spelled as a bare operand, which is vanishingly rare in practice.
# The vocabulary generates them on purpose: a mode that only tried realistic
# input would have been green while `test a -a b` was broken.
#
# FIXED here and now gated (reverting either makes this mode fail):
#   1. A bare-word operand beside a connective was rejected outright —
#      `test a -a b` gave "unknown condition: -a" where zsh gives 0, as did
#      `test x -o x`, `test '' -a ''`, `test a -a b -a c`. c:2486-2492 makes a
#      single-word condition `-n word`, and in C that applies to every operand
#      of a connective because the grammar parses each one; the equivalent
#      rewrite is now done explicitly.
#   2. A four-argument form whose connective followed a `-FLAG operand` pair was
#      rejected as "too many arguments" — `test -n a -a b`, `test -n a -o b`,
#      `test -z '' -a x`, `test -f FILE -a x`. C has no blanket 4-arg rejection.
#
# Any divergence not listed below is a regression.
#
# NOTE on the vocabulary: `<` and `>` are NOT generated even though c:2502-2503
# lists them as three-argument binary operators. They never reach the builtin —
# the shell lexes them as redirections first, so `test b > a` runs `test b` and
# CREATES a file `a` in the harness's cwd; an earlier cut of this mode dropped
# one into the repo root. Quoting does not help: the oracle rejects
# `test a '<' b` with "condition expected: <", so there is nothing to compare.
# `[[ a < b ]]` is where those operators are reachable, and that is the `match`
# mode's surface.
[ ! -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ ! -n ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ '' -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ '' -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -a '' ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -a -n ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -a N ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -a a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -a x ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -o '' ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -o -n ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -o N ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -o a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -a -o x ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -d /nWxistent-zzz -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -d /tmp -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -e /dev/null -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -f /dev/null -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -f /nWxistent-zzz -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -n '' -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -n -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -n -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -n a -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -r /dev/null -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -s /nWxistent-zzz -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -z '' -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ -z a -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ N -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ N -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ a -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ a -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ x -a -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
[ x -o -a ] N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test ! -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test ! -n N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test '' -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test '' -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -a '' N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -a -n N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -a N N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -a a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -a x N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -o '' N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -o -n N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -o N N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -o a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -a -o x N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -d /nWxistent-zzz -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -d /tmp -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -f /dev/null -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -f /nWxistent-zzz -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -n '' -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -n -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -n -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -n a -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -r /dev/null -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -s /nWxistent-zzz -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -z '' -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test -z a -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test N -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test N -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test a -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test a -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test x -a -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
test x -o -a N>&N; print -r -- "rc=$?"
